title: Handling Errors vs Hiding Errors
learningObjectives: Describe the main idea and its role in reliable program behavior.
Recognize the topic in code or a real-world programming scenario.
Trace the relevant behavior and identify the likely outcome.
Explain a common mistake, risk, or limitation.
Apply the concept and verify the result with a suitable check.

understand.concept: Error handling makes failure visible, understandable, and recoverable when appropriate. Error hiding suppresses, ignores, or disguises a failure so the program appears successful or continues with invalid assumptions. Good handling may log safely, show a helpful message, retry under controlled conditions, use a fallback, or stop an operation.
understand.whyItMatters: Hidden failures can corrupt data, mislead users, create security gaps, and make diagnosis difficult. Appropriate handling maintains truthful state and supports safe recovery.
understand.analogy: If a shop cannot process a payment, a responsible cashier explains the issue and offers a safe next step. Pretending the payment succeeded would create a false record. Software should also avoid falsely reporting success.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a simplified comparison; software failures and recovery depend on language, runtime, system boundaries, and context.

explain.narrative: When a failure occurs, determine whether recovery is possible. If so, use a bounded recovery or fallback and make the result explicit. If not, stop the affected operation. Record diagnostic details safely and present a user-appropriate message. Never claim success when the operation failed.

examples.title: Do not swallow exceptions
examples.code: try { JSON.parse('{bad'); } catch(e) { console.log('Could not read settings'); }
examples.explanation: The user sees a truthful message instead of silent failure.

examples.title: Fallback is explicit
examples.explanation: A fallback is safe because it is intentional and documented.

examples.title: Bounded retry concept
examples.explanation: Retry limits prevent an endless retry loop; real retries should include error-specific policy.

examples.title: False success avoided
examples.explanation: UI feedback must reflect the actual outcome.

examples.title: Safe diagnostic
examples.code:
const detail='Request timed out';
console.log('Operation failed: '+detail);
examples.explanation: A diagnostic message preserves actionable context without exposing secrets.

commonMistakes: Empty catch blocks that discard errors.
Showing success UI before an operation is confirmed.
Using an unsafe fallback for data-changing operations.
Retrying forever or retrying non-retryable failures.
Exposing secrets or internal stack traces to end users.
